Both disclosures discuss the Supplementary Leverage Ratio (SLR) requirements for G-SIBs. D427 (2024) details the 5% SLR requirement composed of a 3% minimum and a 2% G-SIB buffer. D416 (2025) details the early adoption of modified eSLR standards replacing the 2% buffer with a buffer equal to 50% of the G-SIB surcharge (Method 1), resulting in a 3.75% SLR requirement. They share the specific topic of SLR requirement components for G-SIBs.

GS attributes this buffer to G-SIB status, while BAC refers to it generally as a 'leverage buffer' but confirms the same 3% + 2% composition for avoiding restrictions on capital distributions and bonuses.

Both firms apply these buffers to satisfy regulatory minimums for holding companies.
